proof_summary: Let \(J(a,b)=\int_0^1 e^x x^a(1-x)^b\,dx\); integration by parts shows that the odd and even linear errors are respectively signed factorial multiples of \(J(m+1,m+1)\) and \(J(m,m+2)\), by matching their recurrences and initial values. Since \(|J(a,b)|\le e\), these errors tend to zero, and positivity (indeed, monotonicity) of the denominators makes the quotient error no larger than the linear error.
